title: Tiferet, the heart of the tree
hookLine: beauty that balances love and strength
carry: tiferet holds love and strength in harmony
last: CHESED GIVES FREELY; GEVURAH GIVES IT SHAPE.

cards: A guitar string tuned too loose just flaps and buzzes. Tuned too tight, it snaps. Somewhere between, there's a point where it rings, and you can hear the moment it arrives.
That point isn't half loose and half tight. It's something else entirely: a note. Love and limits pull in two directions, right arm and left arm.
The kabbalists put a third light in the middle, and they didn't call it compromise, or average, or fairness. They called it beauty.

teach.b: Tiferet. Beauty, glory, harmony. First, where it sits.
On the kabbalists' map, Tiferet stands in the center, below Chesed and Gevurah, holding them together.
Some teachers draw the whole tree in three columns: love on the right, strength on the left, and a middle column running straight down through Tiferet. Second, you've already heard it.
Three days ago, in David's blessing: "the greatness, and the power, and the glory." That word glory, in Hebrew, is tiferet. It was in the list all along.

Micah's verse gave "the mercy to Abraham"; it begins with "the truth to Jacob". Kabbalists link Jacob to Tiferet, and Tiferet to truth: the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham, holding both inheritances in one life.
Truth, in this picture, isn't harsh and isn't soft. It's what you get when love and strength are both honest. Fourth, the surprise.
Harmony here isn't the absence of tension.

teach.h: NOT HALF AND HALF: A CHORD.
teach.b: A chord has notes that differ. A face is beautiful partly because its features aren't all the same.
Tiferet keeps Chesed and Gevurah fully alive and lets them sound together. That's why the kabbalists didn't call it the middle. They called it beauty.
Some teachers also call Tiferet the heart of the map, where the lights meet before they flow on, down toward the world.

how: In Kabbalah, Tiferet is taught as the central sefirah that harmonizes Chesed and Gevurah; Hasidic teaching applies it to a balanced heart, often through the figure of Jacob.

o: a calm middle where neither side gets its way
beauty: love and strength held together at the center
the golden glory of the Temple in old Jerusalem

s: Tiferet means half love and half strength
it's not an average: like a chord, it lets both sound fully together.
the word tiferet is already in David's blessing
"the glory" in 1 Chronicles 29:11 is tiferet in Hebrew.
Micah's verse links Jacob to truth
"the truth to Jacob", the same verse that gives "the mercy to Abraham".

games.q: love pulls one way, limits pull the other. what do the kabbalists put between them?
games.why: they called the center Tiferet, beauty: not an average, but harmony, with both kept alive.

practice: Let your breath be the string: breathe in a little too long and notice the strain, out a little too short and notice the rush, then let it find the length where it rings.
Stay there a while, then bring to mind one part of your life that's too loose or too tight. Don't fix it; just ask what the note would sound like if both sides were honest.

wordCard.voice: Tiferet. Beauty and harmony: the center of the sefirot, holding love and strength together, linked to Jacob and to truth. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: beauty, glory. The sefirah at the center of the map.

carryVoice: Your line: tiferet holds love and strength in harmony. Not half and half, but a chord. Until tomorrow.
